claim: Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts (MEFs) were subjected to glucose deprivation, a stress that causes inhibition of global translation at the initiation and elongation levels mediated by signaling pathways that are AMPK-dependent.
source: Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts (MEFs) were subjected to glucose deprivation, a stress that causes inhibition of global translation at the initiation and elongation levels mediated by signaling pathways that are AMPK-dependent (Bolster et al., 2002; Dubbelhuis and Meijer, 2002; Krause et al., 2002; Reiter et al., 2005; Shenton et al., 2006) and independent (Inoki et al., 2003; Kalender et al., 2010; Sinvani et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research establishing AMPK-dependent mechanisms of translation inhibition during glucose deprivation.

claim: Glucose deprivation causes inhibition of global translation through AMPK-independent signaling pathways.
source: Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts (MEFs) were subjected to glucose deprivation, a stress that causes inhibition of global translation at the initiation and elongation levels mediated by signaling pathways that are AMPK-dependent (Bolster et al., 2002; Dubbelhuis and Meijer, 2002; Krause et al., 2002; Reiter et al., 2005; Shenton et al., 2006) and independent (Inoki et al., 2003; Kalender et al., 2010; Sinvani et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies demonstrating AMPK-independent pathways of translation inhibition.

claim: The ribosome profile in response to glucose starvation showed increased relative amount of 80S monoribosome and decreased polysomal fractions, indicating global inhibition of translation.
source: As expected, the ribosome profile in response to glucose starvation (GS) was dramatically changed as the relative amount of 80S monoribosome was increased while polysomal fractions were decreased (Figure 1B), indicating global inhibition of translation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from polysomal profiling shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 9286 promoters corresponding to 6861 genes had at least 500 reads per promoter in the combined results of two independent experiments.
source: When the results of two independent experiments were combined and normalized using internal controls, 9286 promoters that corresponded to 6861 genes had at least 500 reads per promoter and were considered in further analysis (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of sequencing data from two biological replicates.

claim: Three quarters of the genes had a single expressed promoter in MEF cells and the rest had two or more.
source: Under these thresholds, three quarters of the genes had a single expressed promoter in these cells and the rest had two or more (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Overall translation was reduced upon glucose starvation as evident from the increase and decrease of the polysome-free and polysomal fractions, respectively.
source: We summed all the reads from each fraction for all the promoters and found that the overall translation was reduced upon GS as evident from the increase and decrease of the polysome-free (Free) and polysomal fractions (Heavy), respectively (Figure 1E), consistent with the polysomal profile (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of CapSeq reads across polysomal fractions shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Overall mRNA levels were reduced by approximately 15% after glucose starvation treatment.
source: The overall mRNA levels were reduced by ~15% after the treatment (Figure 1F), which most likely reflect the coupling between translation and mRNA stability (Radhakrishnan and Green, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1F and interpreted in the context of known coupling between translation and mRNA stability.

claim: TOP mRNAs were preferentially inhibited upon glucose starvation on the translational level.
source: As expected, TOP mRNAs were preferentially inhibited upon GS on the translational level (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) while the changes of the mRNA levels were comparable with those of other mRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Following glucose starvation, 22.5% of promoters showed a reduction of two-fold or more in translation.
source: With these settings, we found that following glucose starvation, 22.5% of promoters showed a reduction of two-fold or more in translation whereas only 6.6% of promoters were induced by at least two-fold (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of ribosome occupancy changes shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Following glucose starvation, 6.6% of promoters were induced by at least two-fold in translation.
source: With these settings, we found that following glucose starvation, 22.5% of promoters showed a reduction of two-fold or more in translation whereas only 6.6% of promoters were induced by at least two-fold (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of ribosome occupancy changes shown in Figure 1G.

claim: In basal conditions, 495 pairs of promoters from 327 genes differed in their ribosome occupancy by two-fold or more.
source: In basal conditions 495 such pairs from 327 genes differed in their RO by two-fold or more (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of differential translation between alternative promoters shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Of the differentially translated promoter pairs in basal conditions, 85.5% likely give rise to the same annotated ORF.
source: Of these, the mRNAs of 85.5% of promoter-pairs likely give rise to the same annotated ORF and the rest (14.5%) are predicted to result in proteins with alternative N-termini.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of transcript isoforms and their predicted protein products.

claim: Following glucose starvation, 672 pairs of promoters from 465 genes displayed ribosome occupancy difference of two-fold or more, resulting in 42% increase in differential translation of alternative promoters.
source: When the same analysis was performed following GS, 672 pairs of promoters from 465 genes displayed RO difference of two-fold or more, resulting in 42% increase in differential translation of APs (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of differential translation between alternative promoters under stress conditions.

claim: 70% of differentially translated promoter pairs following glucose starvation do not overlap with those in basal conditions.
source: Interestingly 70% of these differentially translated pairs do not overlap with those in basal conditions (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of differentially translated promoter pairs between conditions shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Among alternative promoters corresponding to the same ORF, those resulting in shorter 5'UTRs had higher ribosome occupancy under basal conditions.
source: Among APs corresponding to the same ORF, those resulting in shorter 5'UTRs had higher RO under basal conditions (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of 5'UTR length and ribosome occupancy shown in Figure 1J.

claim: No significant difference in 5'UTR length was seen between the more and the less efficiently translated promoter pairs following stress.
source: On the other hand, no significant difference in 5'UTR length was seen between the more and the less efficiently translated pairs following stress (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of 5'UTR lengths shown in Figure 1J.

claim: 140 genes had at least one alternative promoter pair that showed ≥2 fold change in mRNA levels in response to stress in both experiments.
source: 140 genes had at least one AP pair that showed ≥2 fold change in mRNA levels in response to stress in both experiments.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of mRNA level changes across alternative promoters.

claim: Of the promoters preferentially induced following stress, 53% encoded a transcript with the same predicted ORF but shorter 5'UTR.
source: Of the promoters preferentially induced following stress, 53% encoded a transcript with the same predicted ORF but shorter 5'UTR while the others were split between transcripts with the same ORF and longer 5'UTR and transcripts with different predicted ORF starts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of stress-induced transcript isoforms shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In MEFs, under basal and glucose starvation conditions, approximately 34% of TSSs initiated with adenosine, 23% with cytidine, 30% with guanosine, and 13% with thymidine.
source: We found that in MEFs, under basal and GS conditions, ~34% of TSSs initiated with adenosine (A), ~23% with cytidine (C), ~30% with guanosine (G) and ~13% with thymidine (T) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), similar to previous reports (Carninci et al., 2006; Yamashita et al., 2006; Forrest et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of TSS nucleotide composition shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and is consistent with prior studies.

claim: Under basal conditions, no significant difference was found in the ribosome occupancy of transcripts that vary in their first nucleotide.
source: Under basal conditions no significant difference was found in the RO of transcripts that vary in their first nucleotide (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of ribosome occupancy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The identity of the first base was correlated with significant differences in the translational response to glucose starvation.
source: In contrast, the identity of the first base was correlated with significant differences in the response to GS (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ribosome occupancy changes shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The ribosome occupancy of transcripts initiating with pyrimidines (C and U) was significantly reduced following glucose starvation while those initiating with purines (A and G) appeared refractory to the stress.
source: The RO of transcripts initiating with pyrimidines (C and U) was significantly reduced while those initiating with purines (A and G) appeared refractory to the stress.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of ribosome occupancy changes by initiating nucleotide.

claim: Under basal conditions, the ribosome occupancy of most trinucleotides is similar, with notable exceptions being UGA, UGC, UGG and UGU that display higher ribosome occupancy.
source: We performed the same analysis for initiating trinucleotides and found that under basal conditions, the RO of most trinucleotides is similar (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B). Notable exceptions are UGA, UGC, UGG and UGU that display higher RO and the pyrimidine-rich trinucleotides CCT, CTC, CTT, that correspond to somewhat lower RO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of ribosome occupancy by initiating trinucleotide shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The pyrimidine-rich trinucleotides CCT, CTC, CTT correspond to somewhat lower ribosome occupancy under basal conditions.
source: Notable exceptions are UGA, UGC, UGG and UGU that display higher RO and the pyrimidine-rich trinucleotides CCT, CTC, CTT, that correspond to somewhat lower RO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B). The latter trinucleotides are most likely part of the TOP (CYYYY) element that was shown to confer slightly reduced translation even under optimal growth conditions (Patursky-Polischuk et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and interpreted in the context of TOP element function.

claim: Following glucose starvation, the majority of trinucleotides with initiating pyrimidines showed reduced translation, while those with purines were largely unaffected.
source: Interestingly following GS (Figure 2C) the majority the trinucleotides with initiating pyrimidines showed reduced translation, while those with purines were largely unaffected (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of ribosome occupancy changes by initiating trinucleotide shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Among the inhibitory trinucleotides following glucose starvation were those that are part of the TOP element such as CCT and CTT, but also others that deviate from the TOP such as CAA, CAT, CTG, TAC.
source: Among the inhibitory trinucleotides were those that are part of the TOP element such as CCT and CTT, but also others that deviate from the TOP such as CAA, CAT, CTG, TAC etc.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of which trinucleotides show translational inhibition following stress.

claim: eIF4E has a single promoter that drives high level of transcription and translation under basal conditions.
source: eIF4E has a single promoter that drives high level of transcription and translation under basal conditions (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Following glucose starvation, eIF4E expression is substantially downregulated at the mRNA and translation levels.
source: Following GS eIF4E expression is substantially downregulated at the mRNA and translation levels (Figure 4A and B), which leads to reduction in eIF4E protein levels (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by CapSeq data (Figures 4A and 4B) and western blot analysis (Figure 4C).

claim: Glucose starvation leads to reduction in eIF4E protein levels.
source: Following GS eIF4E expression is substantially downregulated at the mRNA and translation levels (Figure 4A and B), which leads to reduction in eIF4E protein levels (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The measured Kd for m7GpppG cap analog binding to eIF4E was 561 nM.
source: The measured Kd for the m7GpppG was 561 nM (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is based on intrinsic fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Kd of all capped RNA oligos for eIF4E binding was substantially lower than that of the cap analog, indicating that the RNA moiety increases the binding affinity.
source: Interestingly, under the same conditions, the Kd of all capped RNA oligos was substantially lower, indicating that the RNA moiety increases the binding affinity (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of Kd values from fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Significant differences in the Kd values between capped RNA oligos with different first nucleotides were observed.
source: Furthermore, significant differences in the Kd values between the RNA oligos were observed (Figure 4D, p-values are shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 4D with statistical significance shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The oligo with polypyrimidine CCU as initiating nucleotides displays lower affinity to eIF4E compared to oligos with ACU and GCU as first nucleotides.
source: The oligo with polypyrimidine CCU as initiating nucleotides display lower affinity compared to oligos with ACU and GCU as first nucleotides.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of Kd values from fluorescence measurements.

claim: The Kd values of the mRNAs are correlated with the relationship of the first nucleotides and the ribosome occupancy response to glucose starvation.
source: These Kd values of the mRNAs are correlated with the data of the relationship of the first nucleotides and the RO response to GS (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is based on correlation between binding affinity data and ribosome occupancy data.

claim: Both C-initiated and A-initiated GFP transcripts were downregulated upon eIF4E knockdown, but the effect is substantially more pronounced for the C-initiated transcript.
source: Both, the C and the A initiated transcripts were downregulated but the effect is substantially more pronounced for the C-initiated transcript (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis of GFP expression following eIF4E knockdown shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The C-initiating transcript was much more vulnerable to 4EGI-1 drug treatment compared to the A-initiated one.
source: Here again the C-initiating transcript was much more vulnerable to this drug compared to the A-initiated one (Figure 4F), consistent with the notion that a C as an initiating nucleotide is highly responsive to fluctuations in eIF4E availability.
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis of GFP expression following 4EGI-1 treatment shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Four promoters (p1, p2, p3 and p5) account for most of eIF4A mRNAs.
source: As seen in the mapped CapSeq reads (Figure 5A), four promoters (p1, p2, p3 and p5) account for most of eIF4A mRNAs.
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: p1 and p2 promoters of eIF4A are positioned upstream of the annotated eIF4A protein start codon and in basal conditions these are the major promoters producing highly transcribed and efficiently translated mRNAs.
source: p1 and p2 are positioned upstream of the annotated eIF4A protein start codon and in basal conditions these are the major promoters producing highly transcribed and efficiently translated mRNAs (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: p3 and p5 promoters of eIF4A are intronic and positioned downstream of the annotated protein start codon so that transcription from these promoters generates isoforms with different 5'UTRs and an alternative truncated N-terminus.
source: On the other hand, p3 and p5 promoters are intronic and positioned downstream of the annotated protein start codon so that transcription from these promoters generates isoforms with different 5'UTRs and an alternative truncated N-terminus.
evidence: The claim is based on genomic analysis of promoter positions relative to the coding sequence.

claim: Upon glucose starvation, eIF4A p1 and p2 translation was slightly reduced.
source: Upon GS p1 and p2 translation was slightly reduced (Figure 5B), whereas the intronic p3 and p5 promoters were significantly upregulated transcriptionally and translationally (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Upon glucose starvation, the intronic p3 and p5 promoters of eIF4A were significantly upregulated transcriptionally and translationally.
source: Upon GS p1 and p2 translation was slightly reduced (Figure 5B), whereas the intronic p3 and p5 promoters were significantly upregulated transcriptionally and translationally (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: While p3 and p5 promoters of eIF4A constitute a small fraction of the overall eIF4A under basal conditions, they account for more than half of eIF4A transcripts upon glucose starvation.
source: While p3 and p5 constitute a small fraction of the overall eIF4A under basal conditions, they account for more than half of eIF4A transcripts upon GS.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of CapSeq reads across conditions.

claim: 5'RACE confirmed that eIF4A p3 promoter is strongly induced by glucose starvation.
source: To investigate further the induction of the intronic promoters and their function we first confirmed with 5'RACE that p3 is indeed strongly induced by GS (Figure 5D) and is differentially translated compared to p1 as evident from their distribution in sucrose gradient fractions (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on 5'RACE experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: eIF4A p3 promoter transcript is differentially translated compared to p1 as evident from their distribution in sucrose gradient fractions.
source: To investigate further the induction of the intronic promoters and their function we first confirmed with 5'RACE that p3 is indeed strongly induced by GS (Figure 5D) and is differentially translated compared to p1 as evident from their distribution in sucrose gradient fractions (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on 5'RACE analysis of polysomal fractions shown in Figure 5E.

claim: An energy-stress induced eIF4A polypeptide of 33 kDa that is approximately 13 kDa shorter than the main protein was observed.
source: We observed an energy-stress induced polypeptide of 33 kDa that is ~13 kDa shorter than the main protein (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The truncated eIF4A protein can be synthesized either from Met 121 or Met 127 of the main ORF.
source: This truncated protein can be synthesized either from Met 121 or Met 127 of the main ORF.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed protein size and the sequence of the ORF.

claim: A GFP reporter preceded by the entire novel eIF4A 5'UTR starting from p3 up to Met121 drove the expression of a single polypeptide corresponding to translation initiation at Met121, which was also induced following glucose starvation.
source: We used a GFP reporter that is preceded by the entire novel eIF4A 5'UTR starting from p3 up to Met121. This construct drove the expression of a single polypeptide corresponding to translation initiation at Met121, which was also induced following GS (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis of GFP reporter expression shown in Figure 5G.

claim: N-terminally truncated eIF4A (eIF4AΔN) inhibited GFP protein levels in a dose dependent manner, indicating that eIF4AΔN acts as an inhibitor of eIF4A.
source: While the WT eIF4A has no effect on GFP expression, eIF4AΔN inhibited GFP protein levels in a dose dependent manner, indicating that eIF4AΔN acts as an inhibitor of eIF4A.
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis of GFP expression in the presence of different eIF4A constructs.

claim: The major Pabp promoter under basal conditions is p1, which generates a TOP mRNA.
source: The major promoter under basal conditions is p1, which generates a TOP mRNA (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data and sequence analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Pabp p1 mRNA is expressed 40-folds higher than the next most transcribed isoform, driven by promoter p2.
source: This mRNA isoform is expressed 40-folds higher than the next most transcribed isoform, driven by promoter p2 (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of CapSeq reads shown in Figure 6C.

claim: After glucose starvation, Pabp p1 mRNA levels and translation were both strongly reduced.
source: After GS, p1 mRNA levels and translation were both strongly reduced (Figure 6B and C), while p2 transcription was elevated by eight-fold (Figure 6C) and the vast majority of p2 transcripts were heavily translated (Figure 6B, right).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: After glucose starvation, Pabp p2 transcription was elevated by eight-fold.
source: After GS, p1 mRNA levels and translation were both strongly reduced (Figure 6B and C), while p2 transcription was elevated by eight-fold (Figure 6C) and the vast majority of p2 transcripts were heavily translated (Figure 6B, right).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: After glucose starvation, the vast majority of Pabp p2 transcripts were heavily translated.
source: After GS, p1 mRNA levels and translation were both strongly reduced (Figure 6B and C), while p2 transcription was elevated by eight-fold (Figure 6C) and the vast majority of p2 transcripts were heavily translated (Figure 6B, right).
evidence: The claim is based on CapSeq data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In Pabp, both p1 and p2 are positioned upstream of the annotated protein start codon, hence the differential regulation of the alternative promoters upon glucose starvation changes solely the 5'UTR length (from 467 nt to just 63 nt).
source: In Pabp, both p1 and p2 are positioned upstream of the annotated protein start codon, hence the differential regulation of the APs upon GS changes solely the 5'UTR length (from 467 nt to just 63 nt).
evidence: The claim is based on genomic analysis of promoter positions and resulting transcript structures.

claim: The 5'UTR of the Pabp major isoform consists of conserved A-rich sequences (ARSs) which serve as binding sites of Pabp, resulting in translational repression.
source: Interestingly, it was previously reported by several groups that the 5'UTR of the Pabp major isoform consists of conserved A-rich sequences (ARSs) which serve as binding sites of Pabp, resulting in translational repression (Bag and Wu, 1996; Hornstein et al., 1999; Kini et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research on Pabp autoregulation.

claim: The ARSs are missing in the shorter glucose starvation-induced Pabp mRNA isoform.
source: These ARSs are missing in the shorter GS-induced mRNA isoform.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis of the alternative transcript isoforms.

claim: 5'RACE validated the induction of Pabp p2 mRNA isoform upon glucose starvation.
source: Using 5'RACE we validated the induction of p2 mRNA isoform upon GS (Figure 6D) and the differential translational response of p1 and p2 to GS (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is based on 5'RACE experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 5'RACE validated the differential translational response of Pabp p1 and p2 to glucose starvation.
source: Using 5'RACE we validated the induction of p2 mRNA isoform upon GS (Figure 6D) and the differential translational response of p1 and p2 to GS (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is based on 5'RACE analysis of polysomal fractions shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Despite the strong translational inhibition of the primary Pabp isoform, its protein levels remained stable, suggesting that the highly translated glucose starvation-induced transcript isoform compensates for the diminished translation of transcripts produced from p1.
source: Analysis of Pabp protein levels revealed that despite the strong translational inhibition of the primary isoform its protein levels remained stable, suggesting that the highly translated GS-induced transcript isoform compensates for the diminished translation of transcripts produced from p1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis shown in Figure 6F and interpretation of the data.

claim: Progressive addition of upstream sequences up to 282 nt relative to the initiating ATG of Pabp p2 substantially enhanced Renilla luciferase activity.
source: The results revealed that progressive addition of upstream sequences up to 282 nt relative to the initiating ATG, substantially enhanced RL activity.
evidence: The claim is based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Further extension of Pabp p2 upstream sequences up to 456 nt resulted in diminished Renilla luciferase activity.
source: Further extension of p2 upstream sequences up to 456 nt resulted in diminished RL activity.
evidence: The claim is based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The results confirm that the Pabp p2 promoter overlaps the 5'UTR of the major Pabp transcript and uncovered positive and negative regulatory elements.
source: The results confirm that the p2 promoter overlaps the 5'UTR of the major Pabp transcript and uncovered positive and negative regulatory elements.
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of luciferase reporter assay results.

claim: The 5' ends of mapped reads predominantly corresponded to annotated and CAGE-defined transcription start sites.
source: The 5' ends of mapped reads predominantly corresponded to annotated and CAGE-defined transcription start sites, showing that our methodology provides quantitative single-base resolution view of the TSS landscape (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on metagene analysis shown in Figure 1C validating the CapSeq methodology.

claim: The CapSeq methodology provides quantitative single-base resolution view of the TSS landscape.
source: The 5' ends of mapped reads predominantly corresponded to annotated and CAGE-defined transcription start sites, showing that our methodology provides quantitative single-base resolution view of the TSS landscape (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on validation of the method through comparison with known TSS annotations shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The translation regulatory features following stress differ from those operating in basal conditions.
source: It therefore appears that the translation regulatory features following stress differ from those operating in basal conditions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that 5'UTR length affects translation differently under basal versus stress conditions.

claim: The increase in differential translation of transcript isoforms is part of the cellular stress response.
source: These findings suggest that the increase in differential translation of transcript isoforms is part of the cellular stress response.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that differential translation of alternative promoters increases following stress.

claim: eIF4E binding affinity contributes to the level of translation, in particular when its intracellular concentrations become limiting as in glucose starvation.
source: These findings suggest that eIF4E binding affinity contributes to the level of translation, in particular when its intracellular concentrations become limiting as in GS (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between binding affinity data and translational response, combined with observed reduction in eIF4E levels.

claim: A C as an initiating nucleotide is highly responsive to fluctuations in eIF4E availability.
source: Here again the C-initiating transcript was much more vulnerable to this drug compared to the A-initiated one (Figure 4F), consistent with the notion that a C as an initiating nucleotide is highly responsive to fluctuations in eIF4E availability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing differential sensitivity of C-initiated versus A-initiated transcripts to eIF4E inhibition.

claim: Alternative promoter usage in eIF4A diminishes its activity following glucose starvation, reminiscent of the down regulation of other initiation factors following stress.
source: Thus AP usage in eIF4A diminishes its activity following GS, reminiscent of the down regulation of other initiation factors following stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the stress-induced eIF4A isoform acts as an inhibitor.

claim: The highly translated glucose starvation-induced Pabp transcript isoform compensates for the diminished translation of transcripts produced from p1.
source: Analysis of Pabp protein levels revealed that despite the strong translational inhibition of the primary isoform its protein levels remained stable, suggesting that the highly translated GS-induced transcript isoform compensates for the diminished translation of transcripts produced from p1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Pabp protein levels remain stable despite reduced translation of the major isoform.

claim: As eIF4F activity and the overall mRNA levels are downregulated in response to glucose starvation, the stoichiometry of Pabp relative to eIF4F and to the mRNA poly-A tails is elevated upon the stress and thus contributes to translation inhibition.
source: As eIF4F activity and the overall mRNA levels (dictating the overall abundance of poly-A tails) are downregulated in response to GS, the stoichiometry of Pabp relative to eIF4F and to the mRNA poly-A tails is elevated upon the stress and thus contributes to translation inhibition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Pabp levels remain stable while eIF4F activity and mRNA levels decrease, combined with knowledge that excess Pabp inhibits translation.

claim: Excess of Pabp is inhibitory for translation in vivo and in vitro.
source: However, tight control of Pabp levels is critical as excess of Pabp is inhibitory for translation in vivo and in vitro (Yanagiya et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Pabp plays an important role in translation by promoting RNA circularization mediated by interaction with the cap complex eIF4F.
source: Pabp plays an important role in translation by promoting RNA circularization mediated by interaction with the cap complex eIF4F (Wells et al., 1998; Kaye et al., 2009; Yanagiya et al., 2009; Park et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The truncation of the first 120 amino acids of eIF4A is expected to impair the helicase activity of eIF4A but to retain its interaction with eIF4G1.
source: This truncation is expected to impair the helicase activity of eIF4A but to retain its interaction with eIF4G1 (Dominguez et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is based on citation to prior structural/functional studies of eIF4A.

claim: The TOP element is an uninterrupted stretch of 4–15 pyrimidines, starting with cytidine at the most 5'end of the mRNA.
source: A well-characterized mRNA feature associated with strong translational inhibition is the TOP element (5' Terminal Oligo Pyrimidine), an uninterrupted stretch of 4–15 pyrimidines, starting with cytidine at the most 5'end of the mRNA (for a review see Meyuhas and Kahan [2015]).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge cited from a review.

claim: A large fraction of TOP mRNAs code for proteins that are associated with translation.
source: A large fraction of TOP mRNAs code for proteins that are associated with translation and they are strongly translationally repressed following various physiological stresses that inhibit mTOR signaling by a mechanism that is not fully understood.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about TOP mRNAs.

claim: TOP mRNAs are strongly translationally repressed following various physiological stresses that inhibit mTOR signaling by a mechanism that is not fully understood.
source: A large fraction of TOP mRNAs code for proteins that are associated with translation and they are strongly translationally repressed following various physiological stresses that inhibit mTOR signaling by a mechanism that is not fully understood.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about TOP mRNA regulation.

claim: Under circumstances of limited nutrients or other stresses, mTOR activity is inhibited, 4EBP activity is enhanced and cap-dependent translation is suppressed.
source: Under circumstances of limited nutrients or other stresses mTOR activity is inhibited, 4EBP activity is enhanced and cap-dependent translation is suppressed (Sonenberg and Hinnebusch, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge cited from a review.

claim: 4EBP is controlled by the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), a protein kinase that phosphorylates and diminishes its ability to bind eIF4E.
source: 4EBP is controlled by the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), a protein kinase that phosphorylates and diminishes its ability to bind eIF4E.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about mTOR-4EBP regulation.

claim: Under stress conditions, eIF4E-Binding Proteins (4EBPs) which bind eIF4E with high affinity and interfere with its binding to eIF4G, is activated by dephosphorylation resulting in inhibition of cap-dependent translation.
source: Under these conditions, eIF4E-Binding Proteins (4EBPs) which bind eIF4E with high affinity and interfere with its binding to eIF4G, is activated by dephosphorylation resulting in inhibition of cap-dependent translation.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about 4EBP function.

claim: Stresses such as growth factor, energy and amino acid deficiencies affect the formation of the cap binding complex eIF4F, comprising of the initiation factors eIF4E, eIF4G and eIF4A.
source: Stresses such as growth factor, energy and amino acid deficiencies affect the formation of the cap binding complex eIF4F, comprising of the initiation factors eIF4E, eIF4G and eIF4A.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about stress effects on translation initiation.

claim: The translation inhibition response to stress is mediated by several mechanisms, in particular by the impairment of key initiation factors eIF2 and eIF4E.
source: The translation inhibition response is mediated by several mechanisms, in particular by the impairment of key initiation factors eIF2 and eIF4E (Sonenberg and Hinnebusch, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge cited from a review.

claim: Under stress conditions, translation of many mRNAs is inhibited but that of others is unchanged or even enhanced in order to survive the stress.
source: Under these conditions translation of many mRNAs is inhibited but that of others is unchanged or even enhanced in order to survive the stress.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about differential translation during stress.

claim: Downregulation of the translation machinery is a major mechanism that allows cells to preserve energy and cope with environmental deficiencies.
source: Downregulation of the translation machinery is a major mechanism that allows cells to preserve energy and cope with environmental deficiencies.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about cellular stress responses.

claim: The process of protein synthesis is highly energy consuming and tightly regulated by the availability of nutrients, oxygen and growth factors.
source: The process of protein synthesis is highly energy consuming and tightly regulated by the availability of nutrients, oxygen and growth factors.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about translation regulation.

claim: Recent large-scale promoter analysis in hundreds of human and mouse primary cell types shed light on the prevalence of AP usage in mammals.
source: Recent large-scale promoter analysis in hundreds of human and mouse primary cell types shed light on the prevalence of AP usage in mammals (Forrest et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a large-scale study.

claim: Little is known about the contribution of AP usage to the translational response to stress.
source: Several studies have examined translation and stability of transcript isoforms of the same gene (Arribere and Gilbert, 2013; Floor and Doudna, 2016; Wang et al., 2016) but little is known about the contribution of AP usage to the translational response to stress.
evidence: The claim is based on assessment of the state of knowledge in the field, citing prior studies while noting a gap.

claim: mRNA isoforms with different 5' leaders can vary in their translation efficiency or their half-lives.
source: In addition, mRNA isoforms with different 5' leaders can vary in their translation efficiency or their half-lives.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about mRNA isoform regulation.

claim: Alternative promoter usage can lead to the generation of protein isoforms that differ in their N-termini and as a result have different or even opposite biological functions.
source: Likewise, AP usage can lead to the generation of protein isoforms that differ in their N-termini and as a result have different or even opposite biological functions.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about alternative promoter usage.

claim: The level of transcription initiation can vary between different transcription start sites under different growth conditions, in response to a specific signal or in different cell types and tissues.
source: For example the level of transcription initiation can vary between different transcription start sites (TSS) under different growth conditions, in response to a specific signal or in different cell types and tissues.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about TSS regulation.

claim: Transcription start site (TSS) selection and alternative promoter (AP) usage increase transcriptome diversity and its regulation.
source: Transcription start site (TSS) selection and alternative promoter (AP) usage increase transcriptome diversity and its regulation.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about transcriptome regulation.

claim: The overall mRNA level reduction following glucose starvation most likely reflects the coupling between translation and mRNA stability.
source: The overall mRNA levels were reduced by ~15% after the treatment (Figure 1F), which most likely reflect the coupling between translation and mRNA stability (Radhakrishnan and Green, 2016).
evidence: The claim is speculative interpretation of the observed mRNA reduction, supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: It is possible that the reduction in eIF4E availability by means other than 4EBP may contribute to TOP mRNA regulation.
source: It is possible that the reduction in eIF4E availability by means other than 4EBP may contribute to this regulation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism based on the findings.

claim: It is possible that the signal-modulated trans-acting factors of the TOP element act to modify the eIF4E-mRNA affinity.
source: It is possible that the signal-modulated trans-acting factors of the TOP element act to modify the eIF4E-mRNA affinity.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism for TOP element regulation.

claim: One possibility is that the glucose starvation-induced translational activity of eIF4A p3 involves an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) that can bypass the inhibitory effect of uAUGs.
source: One possibility is that the GS-induced translational activity involves an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) that can bypass the inhibitory effect of uAUGs.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism for translation of the p3 isoform.

claim: Alternatively, translation of eIF4A p3 can be activated by uORF-mediated mechanisms in which phosphorylation of the subunit of eIF2α favors translation of genes containing multiple uAUGs.
source: Alternatively, translation can be activated by uORF-mediated mechanisms in which phosphorylation of the subunit of eIF2α favors translation of genes containing multiple uAUGs (Young and Wek, 2016).
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing an alternative mechanism supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: The translation inhibition of eIF4E may be a backup mechanism for 4EBP-mediated inhibition.
source: The translation inhibition of eIF4E may be a backup mechanism for 4EBP-mediated inhibition.
evidence: The claim is speculative interpretation of the observed eIF4E downregulation.

claim: It is possible that other features in endogenous transcripts may contribute to translation beyond the first nucleotide and isoforms generated from alternative promoters.
source: While the reporter gene assays clearly show the importance of the first nucleotide and isoforms generated from AP for differential translation (Figures 4E, F and 5G), it is possible that other features in endogenous transcripts may contribute to translation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, acknowledging potential additional regulatory features.

claim: eIF4G1 and eIF4A, the partners of eIF4E in eIF4F, may also contribute to the differential affinity via their RNA binding domains.
source: Furthermore eIF4G1 and eIF4A, the partners of eIF4E in eIF4F, may also contribute to the differential affinity via their RNA binding domains.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing potential contributions of other eIF4F components.
